stories.headline: Ukrainian drone threat to Helsinki region triggers emergency alert, airport closure, and government review of warning systems
stories.summary: Early on May 15, Finnish Defence Forces received intelligence that large, explosives-laden Ukrainian drones linked to a major Ukrainian strike operation against Russia might stray into Finnish airspace over the Helsinki-Porvoo corridor. Authorities issued a public emergency alert, told 1.8 million Uusimaa residents to go indoors, and temporarily closed Helsinki-Vantaa airport. PM Orpo was called back from his cottage, Defence Minister Häkkänen authorised use of force, President Stubb contacted Zelensky overnight, and a midday press conference confirmed no drones had entered Finnish territory — though contradictory reports about one possible incursion emerged. Orpo and Häkkänen defended the response as proportionate but acknowledged failures in public communication, promising an SMS-based alert system would be deployed urgently. A parliamentary defence committee hearing with Häkkänen and Interior Minister Rantanen was convened on Tuesday. The Finnish Defence Forces subsequently confirmed the drones came from the Russian direction and were linked to Ukrainian operations.

stories.headline: Opposition files interpellation over government economic failures; Orpo defends austerity record as pre-election battle heats up
stories.summary: Opposition parties filed a joint interpellation in parliament accusing the Orpo government of mismanaging economic policy, including failure to meet its own debt-to-GDP stabilisation target. PM Orpo defended the government's roughly €10 billion in spending cuts as necessary, accused SDP and others of offering no credible alternative, and Finance Minister Purra held firm on fiscal consolidation. The debate produced sharp exchanges about unemployment, tax policy divergence between Kokoomus and SDP, and escalating inter-party rhetoric — including Purra's comment disparaging the Spanish government. Media commentary noted the extraordinarily early start to effective election campaigning ahead of 2027 elections.

stories.headline: PM Orpo's Eurovision flamethrower videos go viral, drawing praise and criticism at home and abroad
stories.summary: PM Orpo posted a series of Instagram videos wielding a flamethrower to support Finland's Eurovision entry Liekinheitin ('Flamethrower') ahead of and after the Vienna final. The videos triggered sharply divided social media reaction in Finland, extensive domestic media coverage of the controversy, and Swedish tabloid Aftonbladet wrote that Orpo had 'jinxed' Finland's chances after Finland finished sixth (behind winner Bulgaria). Post-final, Orpo invited the Finnish duo to his official summer residence Kesäranta.

stories.headline: Stubb calls for Europe to open dialogue with Russia while Ukraine holds strong position; Häkkänen more sceptical
stories.summary: President Stubb made a series of public statements — to an Italian newspaper, Lithuanian media, MTV, LRT, and international outlets — arguing that conditions are approaching for European leaders to resume contact with Moscow, with Ukraine currently in a stronger position than Russia. He stressed any dialogue must start from a position of Ukrainian strength. Defence Minister Häkkänen countered that Russia's full wartime mobilisation shows no genuine interest in peace, while PM Orpo separately noted 'weak signals' of Russian interest in negotiations. The contrast in tone between Stubb and Häkkänen was widely noted.

stories.headline: President Stubb's busy diplomatic week: B9 summit in Bucharest, Lithuania state visit, Europe Gulf Forum in Greece
stories.summary: President Stubb attended the Bucharest Nine (B9) summit in Romania on May 13, where he emphasised NATO unity and Ukraine's role as a security provider, then conducted a state visit to Lithuania (May 14) including a state banquet speech in Vilnius and informal football with children, and subsequently attended the Europe Gulf Forum in Greece on May 16. He also conducted bilateral meetings with Canadian PM Carney, with whom he maintains regular contact on NATO and Ukraine matters.

stories.headline: Finnish public opinion poll: NATO support holds but trust in US has collapsed, majority want less US tech dependence
stories.summary: A new NATOpoll academic survey found strong Finnish support for NATO membership as a security guarantee, but that trust in the US as a reliable ally has fallen sharply — with around four in five Finns wanting to reduce dependence on American weapons and IT technology. Over half favour European nuclear deterrent strengthening and Finnish participation in NATO nuclear exercises. The results were covered across multiple defence and political outlets.

stories.headline: SDP MP Joona Räsänen admits April drink-driving offence, steps back from party positions
stories.summary: SDP MP Joona Räsänen publicly admitted he was stopped by police for drink-driving in Espoo in April and described it as a serious error in judgement. He said he would not seek re-election to the SDP party executive board or the Uusimaa district chairmanship. SDP leader Lindtman and parliamentary group chair Tuppurainen both condemned his conduct, stating it was up to voters to judge him as an MP.

stories.headline: Finnish financial regulator fines Oma Säästöpankki €400,000 for insider register violations
stories.summary: The Finnish Financial Supervisory Authority (Fiva) imposed a €400,000 penalty on Oma Säästöpankki for failing to maintain insider registers in two separate incidents in 2021 and 2022. The cases concerned a software contract termination with Cognizant and a second undisclosed matter. The bank's cooperation with Fiva reduced the fine; Fiva had previously made a police referral regarding the same bank in 2024.
